answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small copper deposit that is locked and slashed on proven duplicate identity. A reputation prism then refracts that stake into separate scores for trading, data, and compute, so one identity cannot borrow trust across domains. New agents start on a narrow ridge with capped volume, and graduate only after verifiable work history. Creating thousands of fake agents would mean locking thousands of deposits and doing real work for each, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once.
